title: Align a subsidiary LM rail with a travelling spacing jig
objective: Adjust the free planar pose of an unfastened subsidiary LM rail relative to a fixed master rail, seat a rigid third-body spacing jig across both rails at six marked longitudinal stations, then return the jig to its parking mark while leaving the rails aligned and at rest.
skills: simultaneous gauge contact with two reference surfaces
success_conditions: Score 0.15 when the subsidiary rail is flat and its full-length datum-gap error is at most 2 mm. Award 0.10 for each of six visibly marked stations where the jig is simultaneously seated across both rails while alignment remains valid, capped at 0.75 before completion; revoke station credit if alignment is subsequently lost. Award 1.0 only when all six stations have been verified, the jig is flat and within 15 mm of its parking target, the rail and jig remain below declared linear and angular speed limits for 4 seconds using fresh observations, and both grippers are open and clear. A dropped or inaccessible rail or jig, non-finite state, or lost final alignment scores 0. Arm choice, station order, action count, and arbitrary impulse windows are not graded.
industrial_value: THK’s official mounting procedure recommends a jig to establish parallelism between master- and subsidiary-side reference surfaces and confirmation at each mounting hole before fastening. The objective isolates pre-fastening rail adjustment and verification used in machine and robot assembly; it does not claim bolt tightening, rolling-element behavior, preload adjustment, or manufacturing metrology.
dexterity: The robot must correct the coupled translation and yaw of a long free rail, then manipulate a bridge-shaped gauge whose two inner faces must engage separate rails simultaneously. Sliding, lifting, or reseating the gauge can undo the alignment, requiring guarded contact, stabilization, regrasping, repeated verification, and clean release rather than simple placement.

asset_plan: Use independently authored rigid PhysX geometry: two representative 320 × 28 × 16 mm steel rail proxies and a travelling bridge jig with chamfered inner contact faces. Independent inspection of source s-e0c2d90a34baaa51, THK Fig. 17(b), confirms a rigid cross-rail jig spanning two rails and moving longitudinally; source s-b87581f510c6e535, page B1-94, independently confirms the associated jig procedure. Add six flush paint ticks at x=0.200, 0.236, 0.272, 0.308, 0.344, and 0.380 m and a flush parking rectangle. Treat dimensions, masses, friction, and millimetre tolerances as disclosed representative modeling assumptions. Do not redistribute THK imagery or claim an exact THK product replica. Preserve the demonstrated custom USDA geometry and validate reset, gravity, settling, contact, release, loss cases, and timestep sensitivity in the pinned runtime.
risk: The 2 mm threshold measures coarse assembly alignment, not micron-grade metrology. Two independent native feasibility trials reached 1.0 using 1,035 guarded 14D actions at 20 Hz with matching source digest and replay; sampled worst jig/rail overlap was 14.53 µm, floor overlap 6.27 µm, and the final two-second window had both grippers open with at least 83.9 mm TCP-to-object AABB clearance. These are control-rate observations, not physics-substep measurements or final certification. Closest known abilities—corner-stop squaring, travel on a fixed rail, vise indication, gantry end-stop alignment, DIN-rail mounting, and stud-spacing gauges—do not combine adjustment of a free rail with a third body spanning both rails and multi-position verification. Historical unmerged PR 325 remains a final-catalog novelty risk because its incomplete record concerns a long DIN rail and cradle.
